_about: Core validation rule library (Phase 1, US v3.2.2 profile). Rules are modelled on the kinds of checks in public agency validation criteria; IDs are the app's own and do not reproduce any agency's numbering. Severity follows the US high/medium/low convention: any High finding means the sequence would likely be technically rejected.

rules.title: Every leaf must reference a file that exists
rules.explain: The backbone points to a document that is no longer in the project's library, so the file would be missing from the package.
rules.fix: Remove the leaf or place a document that exists.

rules.title: No two leaves in a sequence may point to the same file path
rules.explain: Two leaves resolve to the same folder and file name. One file would overwrite the other in the package.
rules.fix: Give one of the documents a distinct file name, or remove the duplicate leaf.

rules.title: Every leaf needs a title
rules.explain: The leaf title is what the reviewer sees in the agency viewer. An empty title makes the document unidentifiable.
rules.fix: Enter a descriptive leaf title in the properties panel.

rules.title: Leaf title should not be the file name
rules.explain: Titles like 'qos_v3_final.pdf' are unhelpful to reviewers and look unprofessional.
rules.fix: Use a readable title, normally the CTD heading or the study title.

rules.title: Regional administrative metadata must be complete
rules.explain: The US regional XML needs applicant, application number, submission type, sub-type and sequence number. Missing values make the sequence unprocessable.
rules.fix: Complete the fields in Module 1 → Regional metadata.

rules.title: Repeatable sections need their attributes
rules.explain: 3.2.S needs substance and manufacturer attributes; 3.2.P needs product name, dosage form and manufacturer. Without them the agency cannot tell repeated sections apart.
rules.fix: Fill the attributes in Project settings → Repeatable sections.

rules.title: File names use lowercase letters, digits and hyphens only
rules.explain: eCTD file names must be lowercase and limited to a-z, 0-9 and hyphen, with a single '.pdf' extension. Spaces, capitals and underscores break the rule.
rules.fix: Rename the file, e.g. 'batch-analyses.pdf'.

rules.title: File names should be 64 characters or fewer
rules.explain: Long file names push folder paths past system limits and are hard to read.
rules.fix: Shorten the file name.

rules.title: Full path should be 180 characters or fewer
rules.explain: The path from the sequence folder to the file is too long and may fail on some systems.
rules.fix: Shorten the file name or repeatable-section folder names.

rules.title: Document is placed under the wrong heading
rules.explain: The document's content belongs to a different CTD section from the node it was placed in. Reviewers will not find it where they expect.
rules.fix: Drag the document to the heading shown in its properties.

rules.title: Heading not used in eCTD
rules.explain: 2.1 (CTD table of contents) is not submitted in eCTD: the backbone is the table of contents.
rules.fix: Remove the leaf from 2.1.

rules.title: PDF version must be 1.4 to 1.7 (or PDF/A-1, PDF/A-2)
rules.explain: Older or newer PDF versions are outside the accepted range for US eCTD.
rules.fix: Re-save the PDF at version 1.7.

rules.title: No security settings or passwords
rules.explain: Secured PDFs cannot be opened, copied or annotated by reviewers.
rules.fix: Remove the document security.

rules.title: All fonts must be embedded
rules.explain: Non-embedded fonts can render incorrectly on the reviewer's machine.
rules.fix: Re-render the PDF with all fonts embedded.

rules.title: Documents of 5 pages or more need bookmarks
rules.explain: Long documents without bookmarks are hard to navigate in review.
rules.fix: Add bookmarks (auto-bookmark from headings).

rules.title: Hyperlinks must resolve
rules.explain: One or more hyperlinks point to a target that is not in the dossier's current view.
rules.fix: Place the target document, or relink the hyperlinks.

rules.title: PDF text must be searchable
rules.explain: Scanned image-only PDFs cannot be searched or copied.
rules.fix: Run OCR or produce the PDF from the source document.

rules.title: Sequence numbers are four digits, unique and in order
rules.explain: Each sequence must have a unique four-digit number, higher than the previous one.
rules.fix: Renumber the sequence.

rules.title: Replace, append and delete need a valid target
rules.explain: The leaf points to an earlier leaf that does not exist, is no longer current, or sits in an earlier sequence that was not submitted.
rules.fix: Choose a current leaf from an earlier published sequence as the target.

rules.title: Lifecycle target must be under the same heading
rules.explain: A replace, append or delete must act on a leaf in the same CTD heading (and the same repeatable section).
rules.fix: Place the new document in the same heading as the leaf it replaces.

rules.title: The first sequence may only use 'new'
rules.explain: There is nothing to replace, append or delete in the first sequence of an application.
rules.fix: Change the operation to 'new'.

rules.title: 'New' leaf duplicates a current leaf
rules.explain: A new leaf with the same title as a current leaf in the same heading usually means 'replace' was intended. The reviewer will now see two versions.
rules.fix: Change the operation to 'replace' and target the earlier leaf.

rules.title: A sequence cannot change after it is published
rules.explain: Published sequences are frozen. Changes need a new sequence.
rules.fix: Create a new sequence for the change.

rules.title: Form FDA 356h is required
rules.explain: Every submission to an NDA includes Form FDA 356h in Module 1.1.
rules.fix: Place the 356h form in 1.1.

rules.title: A cover letter is expected in 1.2
rules.explain: The cover letter tells the review division what the sequence contains and why.
rules.fix: Generate a cover letter in Module 1 and place it in 1.2.

rules.title: User fee coversheet expected for an original NDA
rules.explain: Form FDA 3397 accompanies an original application that is subject to a user fee.
rules.fix: Place Form FDA 3397 in 1.1.

rules.title: Patent information expected for an original NDA
rules.explain: Form FDA 3542a lists patents claiming the drug and is filed with the NDA in 1.3.5.1.
rules.fix: Place the patent information in 1.3.5.1.

rules.title: Debarment certification expected for an original NDA
rules.explain: The applicant certifies it did not use debarred persons, in 1.3.3.
rules.fix: Place the debarment certification in 1.3.3.

rules.title: Financial certification or disclosure expected
rules.explain: Clinical investigators' financial interests are certified or disclosed in 1.3.4.
rules.fix: Place Form FDA 3454/3455 in 1.3.4.

rules.title: Draft labeling expected for an original NDA
rules.explain: Draft prescribing information (1.14.1.3) and carton and container labels (1.14.1.1) are part of an original NDA.
rules.fix: Place both draft labeling documents.

rules.title: Field copy certification expected for an original NDA
rules.explain: Certifies that a field copy of Module 3 was sent to the local office.
rules.fix: Place the field copy certification in 1.3.2.

rules.title: ClinicalTrials.gov certification expected
rules.explain: Form FDA 3674 accompanies applications that contain clinical data.
rules.fix: Place Form FDA 3674 in 1.1.

rules.title: Environmental analysis expected
rules.explain: An environmental assessment or a claim of categorical exclusion goes in 1.12.14.
rules.fix: Place the environmental analysis in 1.12.14.

rules.title: Required heading is empty
rules.explain: This heading is expected for the chosen application type and submission, but has no document in the current view.
rules.fix: Place the matching document from the library.

rules.title: Document is too coarse
rules.explain: One file covers several CTD subsections. Each subsection should be its own document so it can be replaced alone later.
rules.fix: Remove the combined file and place the individual section documents.

rules.title: Document is too fine
rules.explain: The content is split finer than ICH granularity expects, which complicates lifecycle.
rules.fix: Use the single complete document for this heading.

rules.title: Study documents in Modules 4 and 5 need a study tagging file
rules.explain: In the US v3.2.2 profile, every study document in 4.2 and 5.3 is grouped by a study tagging file (STF) that names the study and tags each file's role. Untagged files appear loose in the reviewer's study view.
rules.fix: Give the leaf a study ID and file tag (properties panel), or use 'Tag studies from documents'.

rules.title: File tag must be a valid value for the module
rules.explain: The STF file tag says what the file is (study report, synopsis, protocol…). Tags come from a controlled list and differ between Module 4 and Module 5.
rules.fix: Pick a file tag from the list.

rules.title: Study ID does not match the document
rules.explain: The study ID on the leaf differs from the study the document reports, so the file is grouped under the wrong study.
rules.fix: Use the study ID shown in the document title.

rules.title: Generic drug user fee cover sheet expected
rules.explain: An ANDA includes Form FDA 3794 in Module 1.1.
rules.fix: Place Form FDA 3794 in 1.1.

rules.title: Patent certification is required for an ANDA
rules.explain: An ANDA certifies, for each patent listed for the reference listed drug, under Paragraph I, II, III or IV (or a section viii statement), in 1.3.5.2.
rules.fix: Place the patent certification in 1.3.5.2.

rules.title: ANDA basis for submission statement is required
rules.explain: The basis for submission names the reference listed drug the ANDA relies on, in 1.12.11.
rules.fix: Place the basis for submission statement in 1.12.11.

rules.title: Comparison with the reference listed drug is expected
rules.explain: 1.12.12 compares the generic with the RLD: conditions of use, active ingredient, route, dosage form and strength.
rules.fix: Place the comparison in 1.12.12.

rules.title: Listed drug labeling is expected for an ANDA
rules.explain: An ANDA includes the RLD's labeling and a side-by-side annotated comparison in 1.14.3.
rules.fix: Place both documents in 1.14.3.1 and 1.14.3.3.

rules.title: Form FDA 2252 expected with periodic reports
rules.explain: Annual reports and periodic safety reports for an NDA are transmitted with Form FDA 2252 in 1.1.
rules.fix: Place Form FDA 2252 in 1.1.

rules.title: Cover letter required in 1.0
rules.explain: Every EU sequence includes a cover letter in Module 1.0.
rules.fix: Generate a cover letter and place it in 1.0.

rules.title: Application form required in 1.2
rules.explain: Initial applications and variations include the electronic application form in 1.2.
rules.fix: Place the eAF in 1.2.

rules.title: Product information required in 1.3.1
rules.explain: An MAA includes the SmPC, labelling and package leaflet (English, QRD template) in 1.3.1.
rules.fix: Place the combined product information in 1.3.1.

rules.title: Mock-ups expected in 1.3.2
rules.explain: Mock-ups of the outer and immediate packaging accompany an MAA.
rules.fix: Place the mock-ups in 1.3.2.

rules.title: Expert information expected in 1.4
rules.explain: Signed information about the quality, non-clinical and clinical experts is provided in 1.4.1 to 1.4.3.
rules.fix: Place each expert document.

rules.title: Environmental risk assessment expected in 1.6
rules.explain: An MAA includes an environmental risk assessment, for non-GMO products in 1.6.1.
rules.fix: Place the ERA in 1.6.1.

rules.title: Pharmacovigilance information required in 1.8
rules.explain: An MAA includes the summary of the pharmacovigilance system (1.8.1) and the risk management plan (1.8.2).
rules.fix: Place both documents.

rules.title: Paediatric information expected in 1.10
rules.explain: An MAA for a new medicine includes the PIP decision or waiver and compliance information.
rules.fix: Place the paediatric document in 1.10.

rules.title: Response sequences need a responses document
rules.explain: A sequence with submission unit 'response' carries the responses to the questions in the Responses section.
rules.fix: Place the responses document under Responses.

rules.title: EU Module 1 file names should start with the country code
rules.explain: Files in a country folder are named with that country code first, e.g. ema-cover.pdf or common-responses-maa-d120.pdf.
rules.fix: Rename the file with the country prefix.

rules.title: Related sequence must point to an earlier sequence
rules.explain: Every sequence after the start of a procedure names the sequence that started it (related sequence). Initial and reformat sequences leave it empty.
rules.fix: Set the related sequence in the envelope.

rules.title: Grouped or worksharing submissions list their changes
rules.explain: A grouping covers several changes in one submission; worksharing covers one change across several products. The cover letter and eAF must list them.
rules.fix: List each change (type and scope) in Sequences.

rules.title: Use suspend, not delete or append, in eCTD v4.0
rules.explain: eCTD v4.0 has no delete or append. A context of use is replaced, or suspended to take it out of the current view.
rules.fix: Change the operation to replace, or use Suspend.

rules.title: Sequence numbers in v4.0 are whole numbers starting at 1
rules.explain: The v4.0 sequence number is an integer: the first submission unit is 1, then 2, 3 and so on.
rules.fix: Number the first submission unit 1.

rules.title: Cover letter expected in m1/jp
rules.explain: The PMDA cover letter (cover.pdf) goes in the m1/jp folder; it need not be referenced from the XML.
rules.fix: Generate the cover letter in Module 1.

rules.title: Module 1 table of contents expected
rules.explain: Japanese Module 1 opens with the table of contents for the whole application (1.1).
rules.fix: Place the table of contents in 1.1.1.

rules.title: Copy of the application form required in 1.2
rules.explain: A copy of the Japanese application form goes in 1.2. Brand name and applicant must match the submission unit message.
rules.fix: Place the application form copy in 1.2.

rules.title: Japanese Module 1 item expected
rules.explain: A new drug application in Japan includes patent status, development history, foreign use, similar drugs, the draft RMP and the list of attachments.
rules.fix: Place the missing Module 1 document.

rules.title: Draft package insert required in 1.8
rules.explain: The draft package insert (the Japanese label) goes in 1.8.
rules.fix: Place the draft package insert in 1.8.

rules.title: Modules 1 and 2 must be in Japanese
rules.explain: For Japan, Module 1 and the Module 2 summaries are submitted in Japanese. Modules 3 to 5 may be in English.
rules.fix: Use the Japanese version of the document.

rules.title: Submission unit metadata must match the application form
rules.explain: The brand name and applicant in the submission unit message must match the application form exactly.
rules.fix: Copy the brand name and applicant from the application form.

rules.title: Covering letter required in 1.1
rules.explain: Every submission through the portal opens with a covering letter and, for the application, a comprehensive table of contents.
rules.fix: Generate the covering letter in Module 1.

rules.title: India Module 1 item expected
rules.explain: The India Module 1 asks for the applicant introduction, legal documents, coordinates, QC testing summary, regulatory status and price information.
rules.fix: Place the missing Module 1 document.

rules.title: The right application form is required in 1.2.2
rules.explain: Under the NDCT Rules, 2019, a new drug imported for sale is applied for in Form CT-18; a new drug manufactured in India in Form CT-21.
rules.fix: Place the form that matches the submission type.

rules.title: Fee receipt required
rules.explain: The prescribed fee is paid through the portal and the receipt is part of the application.
rules.fix: Place the fee receipt in 1.2.2.

rules.title: Prescribing information and labels required in 1.3
rules.explain: Draft prescribing information (package insert), labels and cartons are part of the application.
rules.fix: Place them in 1.3.

rules.title: Query response document required
rules.explain: A response to a query letter includes the point-by-point response document.
rules.fix: Place the response under Query Responses.

rules.title: No eCTD lifecycle in a CTD filing
rules.explain: India currently takes CTD dossiers as PDFs through the portal, without an XML backbone, so replace, append and delete have no meaning there. Send the revised document.
rules.fix: Use new.

rules.title: Biosimilar user fee cover sheet expected
rules.explain: A 351(k) BLA includes Form FDA 3792 in Module 1.1.
rules.fix: Place Form FDA 3792 in 1.1.

rules.title: Form FDA 1571 is required for an IND
rules.explain: Every IND submission, initial or amendment, carries Form FDA 1571 in 1.1 (21 CFR 312.23(a)(1)).
rules.fix: Place Form FDA 1571 in 1.1. Form FDA 356h is for marketing applications.

rules.title: Form FDA 1572 expected for each investigator
rules.explain: The investigator's statement on Form FDA 1572 commits each clinical investigator to the IND regulations.
rules.fix: Place Form FDA 1572 in 1.1.

rules.title: Introductory statement and general investigational plan expected
rules.explain: An initial IND explains the drug, the rationale and the plan for the coming year (21 CFR 312.23(a)(3)); the US Module 1 holds it in 1.20.
rules.fix: Place the general investigational plan in 1.20.

rules.title: Investigator's brochure expected
rules.explain: The investigator's brochure (21 CFR 312.23(a)(5)) sits in 1.14.4.1.
rules.fix: Place the investigator's brochure in 1.14.4.1.

rules.title: Form FDA 3938 is required for a DMF submission
rules.explain: FDA provides Form FDA 3938 as the standard form for DMF submissions.
rules.fix: Place Form FDA 3938 in 1.1.

rules.title: Patent certification for the listed drug is required in a 505(b)(2) NDA
rules.explain: A 505(b)(2) application that relies on a listed drug certifies to each patent listed for it (Paragraph I to IV, or a section viii statement), in 1.3.5.2.
rules.fix: Place the patent certification in 1.3.5.2.

rules.title: Reference and concerned member states must be named
rules.explain: A decentralised or mutual recognition procedure has one reference member state (RMS) and at least one concerned member state (CMS); a national procedure names the member state. Each receiving state gets its own envelope.
rules.fix: Set the RMS and CMSs in Module 1.

rules.title: National product information needed for every receiving member state
rules.explain: Outside the centralised procedure, 1.3.1 holds product information per member state, in a country folder and a language folder (m1/eu/13-pi/131-spclabelpl/CC/LL/).
rules.fix: Place each member state's product information in 1.3.1.

rules.title: The 'ema' folder is only for the centralised procedure
rules.explain: Country folder 'ema' identifies documents for the EMA. In a decentralised, mutual recognition or national procedure, documents go in the member state's folder or 'common'.
rules.fix: Remove the EMA document and use the member state's version.

rules.title: ASMF documents must say whether they are AP or RP
rules.explain: The ASMF eCTD guideline asks for 'AP' or 'RP' in the substance metadata and in every leaf title in 2.3.S and 3.2.S, and recommends an -ap or -rp suffix on file names.
rules.fix: Add AP or RP to the leaf title and file name.

rules.title: Restricted information placed in the applicant's part
rules.explain: The restricted part (detailed route of synthesis, materials, critical steps, process validation) is confidential to the authorities. In the applicant's part the MA applicant would see it.
rules.fix: Remove it from the AP and file it in the RP.

rules.title: Information about the quality expert expected
rules.explain: An ASMF includes information about the expert in Module 1.4.1.
rules.fix: Place the expert information in 1.4.1.
